ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in an equilateral triangle $ABC$ with side length $9$, where $BD=3$, and $\angle ADE=60^\circ$, what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, we have $\angle B=\angle C=60^\circ$, and $AB=BC$.\\
Therefore, $CD=BC-BD=9-3=6$, and $\angle BAD+\angle ADB=120^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle ADE=60^\circ$, $\angle ADB+\angle EDC=120^\circ$. Thus, $\angle DAB=\angle EDC$.\\
Moreover, since $\angle B=\angle C=60^\circ$, we conclude that $\triangle ABD\sim \triangle DCE$.\\
Thus, $\frac{AB}{BD}=\frac{DC}{CE}$, which gives $\frac{9}{3}=\frac{6}{CE}\Rightarrow CE=2$.\\
Therefore, $AE=AC-CE=9-2=\boxed{7}$.
